summary: Heatmap tab: a movable density grid over a region of the level, doubling as a measuring grid.
overview: Answers a whole-level question rather than a per-object one: is my level evenly built. Over-decorated clusters and barren dead zones are near-impossible to notice while you are zoomed in placing individual props, and both matter — barren patches read as unfinished, and dense clusters hurt readability and are exactly where draw calls concentrate.

It also does double duty as a ruler, on purpose. Cell size is entered in a unit you pick, shared with the Measuring Tape tab, so a corridor spanning three 2-metre cells reads as 6 metres wide without measuring anything.

walkthrough.step: Select something in the area you want to inspect and press Center Region On Selection.
walkthrough.whatYouSee: A sized box snaps over it with a Scene-view move handle, so you position the region by dragging rather than guessing at extents.

walkthrough.step: Set the region's X and Z for the footprint, and Y for the height slice.
walkthrough.whatYouSee: Only objects whose CENTRE sits inside that height are counted, which is how you isolate one storey of a stacked level. The grid itself draws at the BOTTOM of the region, so put the box on the floor you are inspecting.
The whole rectangle fills in, empty cells included, so it reads as one continuous grid rather than scattered patches.

walkthrough.step: Pick a metric: Bounds Volume or Object Count.
walkthrough.whatYouSee: Bounds Volume answers 'how visually heavy is this area', which is usually the more meaningful question — one large building and one pebble are not the same amount of level. Object Count is a plain tally.

walkthrough.step: Set Density Max to the density that should count as fully red.
walkthrough.whatYouSee: A fixed scale you chose, not one auto-fitted to the busiest cell. Auto-fitting would paint the single busiest cell red in an almost-empty level and tell you nothing.

walkthrough.step: Turn on Drape On Floor for uneven ground.
walkthrough.whatYouSee: Each cell raycasts down so the grid follows terrain instead of sitting on one flat plane. It costs one raycast per cell, on rebuild only.

useCases: Finding the wing of a level that is visibly under-dressed compared to the rest.
Spotting prop clusters that will concentrate draw calls before they become a performance problem.
Using round cell sizes as an on-screen ruler while blocking out corridors and rooms.
Inspecting one floor of a multi-storey building without the floors above and below confusing the reading.

gotchas.title: The grid is cached, not live
gotchas.body: It rebuilds on demand and when the hierarchy actually changes — never per repaint, and it never forces continuous Scene-view redraws. Moving objects does not continuously recolour it; press Build / Refresh Grid for the current picture.

gotchas.title: Density Max changes the story the colours tell
gotchas.body: Set it once for a given level's scale and leave it alone, or two readings taken on different days are not comparable. Too high and a genuinely dense area reads as mild; too low and everything saturates to red.

gotchas.title: The Y size is a filter, not just a box height
gotchas.body: An object is counted only if its centre falls inside the region's height. A very tall object whose centre sits above the slice will not be counted even though it passes through the area.
